metadata.name: MGFA Clinical Classification (Myasthenia Gravis)
metadata.summary: Standardized clinical classification (Class I–V) of Myasthenia Gravis by distribution and severity of muscle weakness.
clinical_pearls: Assign class based on the patient's worst clinical status (or current status with explicit notation); pair with MG-ADL for longitudinal symptom tracking.
Subtype 'a' denotes predominantly limb/axial weakness; subtype 'b' denotes predominantly oropharyngeal/respiratory weakness.
Pitfall — Subjective grading & low sensitivity: Separating mild (II), moderate (III), and severe (IV) weakness is subjective, limiting interrater agreement and sensitivity to small clinical changes.

Pitfall — Staging vs outcome tool: MGFA Clinical Classification is a baseline/worst-status staging system rather than an outcome measure; use MGFA Post-Intervention Status (PIS) to assess treatment response and do not use it to directly compare severity across patients.

options.label: Any ocular muscle weakness (may have eye closure weakness); all other muscle strength is normal
Mild weakness affecting other than ocular muscles; predominantly affecting limb, axial muscles, or both
Mild weakness affecting other than ocular muscles; predominantly affecting oropharyngeal, respiratory muscles, or both
Moderate weakness affecting other than ocular muscles; predominantly affecting limb, axial muscles, or both
Moderate weakness affecting other than ocular muscles; predominantly affecting oropharyngeal, respiratory muscles, or both
Severe weakness affecting other than ocular muscles; predominantly affecting limb, axial muscles, or both
Severe weakness affecting other than ocular muscles; predominantly affecting oropharyngeal, respiratory muscles, or both
Defined by intubation, with or without mechanical ventilation (except during routine postoperative management)

interpretation.label: Class I — Purely Ocular MG
interpretation.summary: Weakness restricted to extraocular muscles (diplopia, ptosis) and orbicularis oculi; no generalized or bulbar involvement.

interpretation.label: Class II — Mild Generalized MG (IIa / IIb)
interpretation.summary: Mild generalized weakness; Class IIb indicates predominant bulbar/respiratory involvement requiring closer monitoring.

interpretation.label: Class III — Moderate Generalized MG (IIIa / IIIb)
interpretation.summary: Moderate generalized weakness; Class IIIb patients with dysphagia/dysarthria or dyspnea carry elevated crisis risk.

interpretation.label: Class IV — Severe Generalized MG (IVa / IVb)
interpretation.summary: Severe generalized weakness; Class IVb warrants urgent ICU-level respiratory monitoring and rapid immunotherapy (IVIG/PLEX).

interpretation.label: Class V — Myasthenic Crisis (Intubated)
interpretation.summary: Intubation required for respiratory failure or airway protection; manage in ICU with IVIG or plasmapheresis.

assessment_guides.title: Distinguishing Subtypes 'a' vs 'b' & Class V
bedside_steps: Determine whether any non-ocular muscles are weak (if only ocular/eyelid closure -> Class I).
Grade overall non-ocular severity (Mild = II, Moderate = III, Severe = IV).
Assign 'a' if limb/axial weakness predominates, or 'b' if oropharyngeal/respiratory weakness predominates (even if limb weakness is also present).
pitfalls_and_exceptions: Use of a feeding tube without intubation classifies the patient as Class IVb, not Class V.
Routine postoperative intubation after thymectomy does not automatically assign Class V unless prolonged/crisis-related.

references.citation: Jaretzki A 3rd, Barohn RJ, Ernstoff RM, et al. Myasthenia gravis: recommendations for clinical research standards. Task Force of the Medical Scientific Advisory Board of the Myasthenia Gravis Foundation of America. Neurology. 2000;55(1):16-23.
Benatar M, Sanders DB, Burns TM, et al. Recommendations for myasthenia gravis clinical trials. Muscle Nerve. 2012;45(6):909-917.
